title: Moving from guitar to violin and cornet
summary: He began guitar around 17, found it too slow, took up violin and later bought a cornet; he played guitar alone at first.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Yeah, before I took up the violin. Then I take the violin. But the cornet, I didn't take it. I know the music. Yeah. All I had to do, by a method. And, uh, at the, uh, fainting, you understand? Get the tone, A, B, you know, after I got the tone, I know the music, that's all. I just wanted to know the scales. Yeah. Right. So about how old were you when you started on, uh, guitar? When I was about, uh, I was about 17 years old.
17. Yeah. And then, uh, how late did you start on the violin? How much later did you start on the violin?

Well, afterwards, uh, the guitar was too slow. And I went and got the violin. So I left the band for about, oh, about six or seven years. And then, uh, it got a little too slow. So I went and bought a cornet.
Yeah. Did you play guitar in the band then too, when you took that violin?
Well, I could play it, but I never did, uh, uh, I hired somebody else. Just after I took the violin. Yeah. Uh, it was the lead, you see.
I mean, when you started on guitar, were you playing with other people or did I play yourself?
No, no. I was by myself.
